sentences.text: 1  CAV JUDGMENT 1.

By way of present petition under Articles 226 & 227 of the Constitution, petitioner challenges order dated 04.10.2011 passed by HC-NIC Page 1 of 5 Created On Fri Aug 14 12:50:34 IST 2015 learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No.8, Ahmedabad in Criminal Case No.4383 of 2008 wherein learned Magistrate rejected application below Exh.36 seeking directions to the Prosecution to adduce evidence in the form of examination-in-chief afresh by examining witnesses in the Court.
2. Rule.
Learned counsels appearing for respondents waive service of Rule.

3. Facts giving rise to this petition are that the petitioner was convicted by learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No.8, Ahmedabad in Criminal Case No.4383 of 2008 vide order dated 18.5.2010 for the offence punishable under section 7 (2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and imposed punishment to remain present in the Court till rising of the Court and also imposed fine of Rs.4,000/-, in default to undergo imprisonment for seven days.

Respondent No.1 (State) challenged the aforesaid order before this Court by way of filing Criminal Appeal No.123 of 2011 and, after hearing the parties, this Court partly allowed the appeal by quashing and setting aside order dated 18.5.2010 passed by learned Metropolitan Magistrate and the matter was remanded back to the trial Court for fresh trial in accordance with law.
4.

When the proceedings started before the trial Court afresh, prosecution moved an application that examination-in-chief of their witnesses recorded earlier be taken into consideration while HC-NIC Page 2 of 5 Created On Fri Aug 14 12:50:34 IST 2015 conducting fresh trial as per the directions of this Court.
This application was opposed by the original accused on the ground that decision on the basis of examination-in-chief recorded earlier will adversely affect the rights of the accused.
Metropolitan Magistrate allowed the application of the State by holding that examination-in- chief recorded earlier will be taken into consideration while recording evidence.

Aggrieved from this order, petitioner has preferred present petition on the ground that petitioner will be deprived of his valuable right in case the examination-in-chief recorded in the Court is relied upon by the prosecution.
5. I have heard learned counsels appearing on both sides and have also gone through the judgment/order dated 28.3.2011 passed by this Court.

6. Main grievance of the petitioner in this case is that the witnesses earlier examined by the prosecution be summoned in the Court and their evidence be recorded afresh as, while remanding this case, there were directions of the High Court for fresh trial.
7. Generally, accused cannot agitate if examination-in-chief recorded earlier by the prosecution is relied upon and witnesses are made available for the purpose of cross-examination by the defence.
However, present case has peculiar facts.

Vide judgment dated 28.3.2011 passed in Criminal Appeal No.123 of 2011, the case has HC-NIC Page 3 of 5 Created On Fri Aug 14 12:50:34 IST 2015 been remanded and is ordered to be tried afresh for the reason that in the earlier proceedings before Shantilal Dahyabhai Vora vs Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation & on 12 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72691231/
2 learned Magistrate, though the accused were held guilty, yet the sentence imposed upon the petitioner was less than the minimum prescribed under the Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The State has come in appeal against this order and while disposing of this appeal, aforementioned order has been passed by this Court.
As could be seen, the dispute was only regarding quantum of sentence.
There was no controversy between the parties as far as conviction part was concerned.
In this view of the situation, even cross- examination and finding recorded by learned Metropolitan Magistrate regarding holding the accused guilty was not required to be reviewed.
Only the sentence part was required to be reviewed as the punishment imposed upon the accused/petitioner was less than the minimum prescribed under the Act.

8. This Court is of the view that the grievance of both sides will be redressed if the earlier conviction order passed by learned Magistrate is maintained and appropriate sentence upon the accused is passed afresh in accordance with law.
This is particularly so when the conviction recorded by learned Metropolitan Magistrate is not challenged by the accused and they have accepted the order.
It was only the State who was aggrieved from sentence part as it was less than the minimum prescribed under law.
HC-NIC Page 4 of 5 Created On Fri Aug 14 12:50:34 IST 2015 9.
Resultantly, this appeal is partly allowed.
The conviction recorded against the accused shall remain intact.
However, the sentence portion is quashed and set aside.
The Metropolitan Magistrate will pass fresh sentence upon the accused in accordance with law.
Rule is made absolute in the above terms.

Sd/-
